E12_false_alarm.v: No real-time monitoring, ARL0 or FPR analysis in this WP version (the published JFEC 2012 version adds a CUSUM monitoring procedure per the journal abstract). Family-wise false detection across the recursive sequence is handled by sup-functional statistics with simulated finite-sample CVs; empirical family-wise size at 5% under the no-bubble DGP: 0.041-0.053. The dating rule tauP1 uses the pointwise asymptotic DF critical value 1.28 (eq.20) with no multiplicity adjustment; tauP2 uses the 5% supDF CV.

E13_validity.v: Model (11): time-varying AR(1), epsilon_t white noise with E(eps)=0, E(eps)^2=sigma^2, y0=c<infinity; no constant/drift in the model (a possible constant handled by prior detrending on constant + linear trend); null H0: rho_t=1 for all t (eq.12). Minimum window: tau0=0.2 for the supDF forward recursion, tau0=0.1 for supB/supBT/supK/supDFC. Limit distributions derived as Wiener functionals (supB/supBT/supK via CMT, pp.6-7; supDFC in Proposition 1 p.8); finite-sample CVs simulated (10.000 reps). Finite-sample caveat: supDFC CVs depend on the initial value if the series is not detrended, so supDFC is applied to y_t - y_0 (p.12). Homoskedastic errors only; no non-stationary-volatility robustness analysis. Reported failure: break-type tests (supDFC/supBT/supB) lose power against periodically collapsing bubbles when collapses occur in the last sample part (Evans critique), e.g. rejection <10% at pi=0.85.
E13_validity.loc: sec.3 pp.4-8; Proposition 1 p.8; sec.6.1 p.12; sec.6.3 p.17

Values (0.001/0.01/0.05): rho1=0.5 at tau-1: 0.0003/0.0073/0.0371; rho1=0.9 at tau-1: 0.0013/0.0131/0.0525; rho1=1.0 at tau-1: 0.0027/0.0124/0.0529; rho1=1.0 at tau-3: 0.0018/0.0138/0.0573 (largest 5% entry in table); joint rejections much smaller, e.g. rho1=1.0 tau-1&tau-2 at 5%: 0.0094; tau-1,tau-2,tau-3: 0.0012. E11_dating.v: not reported. No origination/termination date estimator and no bias/MAE/RMSE/delay distributions; the design instead tabulates rejection frequencies at fixed pre-collapse test dates tau-1, tau-2, tau-3 (1-3 periods before the collapse), an early-warning measure rather than dating accuracy.

E12_false_alarm.v: No formal FWER control or ARL0. Sequential use addressed empirically: Table 1 reports joint false-rejection frequencies over consecutive test dates (tau-1 and tau-2; tau-1, tau-2 and tau-3), e.g. at 5% for rho1=1.0: single dates 0.0529-0.0573, two dates 0.0094, three dates 0.0012; the 0.1% and 1% levels are included because 'one may want to use a sequence of test values in practice'.

E13_validity.v: 'No new asymptotic theory is needed, nor new simulated critical values, as the test statistic asymptotically obeys a normal distribution' (sec.4 p.6). Derivation assumes an ARMA process phi(L)y_t = theta(L)eps_t with white-noise eps_t (mean zero, variance sigma_eps^2); the balance coefficient 0.5 in (1-L)y_t - 0.5(1-L)^2 y_t = 0.5(1-L^2)y_t follows analytically ((sigma^2+2sigma^2)/(6sigma^2)=0.5) and is not estimated; test = one-step-ahead forecast errors from recursive residuals of regressing (1-L^2)y_t on an intercept (Eviews recursive estimation); lags may be added for residual autocorrelation. Robustness gaps stated by the author: the test 'might also be modified to allow for ARCH like patterns' before applying to higher-frequency financial data (p.7); simulations use homoskedastic Gaussian errors only; power falls substantially when the error SD rises from 500 to 2000 (Table 3) and when the test sample shrinks from 70 to 40 observations (Table 4).
E13_validity.loc: sec.2 pp.3-4; sec.4 pp.6-7; Tables 3-4 pp.25-26

Q1.g: Null = stability of (1-L^2)y_t (growth-acceleration balance) with intercept-only regression stated; critical values from stated asymptotic normality of the recursive-residual statistic (sec.4 p.6).

Q2.g: Empirical size at 0.1%/1%/5% under a fully parameterized null DGP (rho1 in {0.5,0.9,1.0}), test sample 70, 10000 reps (Table 1 p.23).

Q3.g: Power under explicit explosive alternatives rho1 in {1.01,1.02,1.03,1.05,1.10} with all DGP parameters stated (Tables 2-4).

Q4.g: The DGP contains a single collapse at tau (switch to beta2=10000, rho2=0.5), but rejection is evaluated only at pre-collapse dates tau-1..tau-3, so no collapsed observations enter the tested data; no periodically-collapsing alternative.

Q5.g: No dating estimator; only rejection frequencies at fixed dates 1-3 periods before collapse, no bias/MAE/RMSE/delay distributions.

Q6.g: Recursive residuals use only data through t (one-step-ahead forecast errors); fixed normal critical values; explicitly framed as timely monitoring of an ongoing series.

Q7.g: Sequence multiplicity addressed empirically: joint false-rejection rates over consecutive test dates reported (Table 1 p.23) and stricter 0.1%/1% levels motivated for sequential use; no formal FWER theory.

E9_size.v: No size table. Prose/figure evidence only: constant-SE version - pre-bubble (t<3000) per-observation signal frequency 'moving around 5%' at the 5% level and 'around 5%' until t=3500 (Figure 12); on real IPO data, stable periods show few false signals, some at sudden price changes at 5%, 'almost neglectible' at 0.1% (sec.3.2 p.12). GARCH-SE version on real data 'provides signals in almost every period ... We can therefore conclude that the size of the test is very low' [sic - wording as printed, describing over-signalling] (sec.3.2 p.14 area), while in simulations its pre-bubble rate is ~5% (Figure 13).

E10_power.v: 100 Monte Carlo replications (computational constraint, sec.4.1). DGP eqs (10)-(12): p_t = p^f_t + b_t; p^f_t random walk with drift alpha0=0 and GARCH(1,1) errors gamma0=0.0001, gamma1=0.06, gamma2=0.93 (parameters estimated from 5000 seconds of LinkedIn IPO-day prices via a state-space approach); bubble b_3000=0.25, growth g=0.005, b_t=(1+g)b_{t-1} for t in [3000,4000], 0 otherwise; T=5000. Per-t signal frequency (power), 5% level, constant-SE version (Figure 12): ~0.05 pre-bubble; spike ~0.5 at t=3000 (initial bubble jump); ~0.05 until t=3500; rising to ~0.7 just before the collapse ('signals hinting towards a collapse in more than 50% of the cases'); exactly 0 from t=4001 onward. GARCH-SE version (Figure 13): stays ~0.05 and even decreases during the bubble - 'using GARCH standard errors makes the test useless'. 1% and 0.1% versions in appendix Figures 18-21 show the same pattern at lower levels. All values read from prose/figures; no numeric tables.
E10_power.loc: sec.3.3 pp.14-18; Figures 12-13 pp.17-18; Figures 18-21 pp.28-31

E11_dating.v: not reported. No origination/termination dating estimator, no detection-delay distribution; only per-observation signal frequencies over time in figures.

E12_false_alarm.v: No ARL0/FWER treatment. Prose: in relatively stable periods 'the test does not provide us with false signals'; at 5% some false signals at sudden price changes, at 0.1% 'almost neglectible' (sec.3.2 p.12). Post-collapse signal rate exactly 0 from t=4001 (standard errors inflated by the bubble period), flagged as a problem for periodically collapsing bubbles with suggested remedy of excluding data before/during a previous bubble (sec.3.3 pp.17-18).

E13_validity.v: Recursive residuals w_t (eq.7) independently N(0, sigma^2) under stability with homoskedastic errors; balance regression coefficient (eq.5) = (sigma^2_t + 2 sigma^2_{t-1})/(sigma^2_t + 4 sigma^2_{t-1} + sigma^2_{t-2}), equal to 0.5 under homoskedasticity and approximately 0.5 in the limit under conditional heteroskedasticity; GARCH(1,1) model eqs (8)-(9) (Bollerslev). Documented robustness failure: replacing constant SEs with one-step-ahead predicted GARCH SEs makes the test unable to detect explosive behavior (recursive residuals stay inside the widened GARCH bands: Figures 5, 8, 11, 13); the GARCH-SE variant is more accurate only for stable processes. Only 100 MC replications; author recommends >=1000 (sec.4.1).

Q1.g: Null = stability of the (1-L^2)y_t regression; recursive residuals stated to be independently normal with zero mean and regression variance (p.7), giving the 2-SE / 95-99-99.9% normal bands their provenance.

Q2.g: No tabulated empirical size under the stated null DGP; only a visual ~5% pre-bubble signal rate (Figure 12) and qualitative prose.

Q3.g: Explicitly parameterized explosive alternative: b_t=(1+g)b_{t-1}, g=0.005, b_3000=0.25, GARCH(1,1) parameters given (eqs 10-12, pp.14,17).

Q4.g: The bubble collapses in-sample at t=4000 (b_t=0 afterward) and post-collapse behavior is analyzed; single collapse, not an Evans-type periodically collapsing process.

Q5.g: No dating accuracy or delay distributions; per-observation signal frequencies in figures only.

Q6.g: Recursive-residual statistic at t uses data through t only; fixed normal bands; explicit real-time prediction/monitoring framing.

Q7.g: No family-wise control or ARL0 for the per-second signal sequence; only informal reliance on stricter 1%/0.1% levels to limit false signals.

E13_validity.v: Null DGPs: eqs [1]-[2] (fixed-magnitude drift break, eps ~ IID(0,sigma^2)) under which DF_mu diverges to +/-infinity (point-mass limit, size tends to 1 or 0); and eqs [4]-[6] (break local to zero, alpha2*T^-1/2) with the non-degenerate limit in Theorem 1: DF_mu => (sigma^2+c2)^{1/2}[sigma^2 int W~^2 dr + c3 + 2 l3]^{-1/2}[sigma^2 int W~ dW + c1 + l1 + l2], with c1=sigma^2 k^2 lambda(1-lambda)^2/2, c2=0, c3=sigma^2 k^2 {[(1-lambda)^3/3]-[(1-lambda)^4/4]}; as k->0 the usual DF (and PWY) distributions are recovered. Model includes constant only, no deterministic trend (following PSY that a trend is empirically unrealistic in right-tailed testing); first-order dynamics; alpha1=0 throughout; tau0=0.10; SDF_mu asymptotics eq.[13] combine Theorem 1 with PWY limit theory. Documented failure: positive size distortion / spurious rejections in favour of the explosive alternative up to 1.000 unless the break is small and late (Tables 1-2); asymptotic densities shift rightward with break size, worst for mid-sample breaks (Figures 1-8). Generalization to PSY local-to-zero drifts eqs [17]-[19] noted; remedies discussed (Perron AO endogenous break; break dummies from LS break-fraction estimate eq.[21], at a power cost if no break).

E11_dating.v: Core results. Metric: simulated frequency that estimated dates fall within k in {0,1,5} observations of the true b(tau1,0)Tc and b(tau2,0)Tc, conditional on PSY rejection at the 0.05 level; T=200, 2,000 reps, v_t ~ IIDN(0,1), bubble timing tau1,0=0.5, tau2,0=0.7 (duration 0.2T), collapse tau3,0=0.8 (duration 0.1T), bubble magnitude grid delta1 in {0.0400, 0.0425, ..., 0.1000}, collapse magnitude delta2 in {delta1/2, delta1}; BICopt trimming s=0.1. Results presented graphically only (Figures 1-3; no numeric tables). Prose anchors: BICopt start-date accuracy markedly above PSY for all k; BICopt end-date exact-hit (k=0) frequency 'close to one for the larger values of delta1' (DGP 2, Figure 1); PSY end-date frequencies 'at, or ... very close to, zero for much of the delta1 range' for k=0 and k=1; PSY end date systematically delayed relative to the true termination; only for k=5 under the faster collapse (delta2=delta1, Figure 3) does PSY reach similar accuracy to BICopt. Correct-model-selection frequencies in Figure 4 (increasing in delta1; best for DGP 1, worst for DGP 4). Asymptotics: exact-date consistency b(tauhat_i)Tc - b(tau_i,0)Tc ->p 0 for correct DGP/Model pairs (Theorem 1). Empirical application (Table 1, Nasdaq 1973:2-2005:6, T=389, s=0.05): PSY dates 1998:11-2000:12 vs BICopt Model 3 dates 1998:11-2000:9; pseudo real-time: BICopt flags termination when the sample reaches 2000:12 (end date 2000:9) while PSY gives a clear termination signal only at 2001:3.

E12_false_alarm.v: not reported (no ARL0/false-alarm rate study). Episode-level safeguards in the PSY comparator implementation: a valid bubble episode requires at least floor(ln T) contiguous BSADF rejections, and when multiple episodes are flagged the longest contiguous rejection sequence is used for dating.

E13_validity.v: Assumption 1: v_t = C(L)eps_t linear process; eps_t IID, mean zero, unit variance, finite fourth moment; summability sum j|C_j| < infinity, C(1)^2 > 0; homoskedastic. Initial condition u1 = Op(1). Regimes of O(T) duration; trimming tau1 >= s, tau2 - tau1 >= s, tau3 - tau2 >= s/2 with s=0.1 (s=0.05 in the T=389 application). Collapse-dominance condition (2): (1+delta1)^(tau2,0-tau1,0)*(1-delta2)^(tau3,0-tau2,0) >= 1 required for exact-date consistency of the collapse end (otherwise only break-fraction consistency). Stated conjecture (not proved): consistency and BICopt selection results 'will continue [to] hold under most forms of heteroskedasticity, including nonstationary volatility', because only stochastic orders of magnitude are involved (sec.4 p.10). PSY implementation: fixed lag 1, minimum window floor((0.01+1.8/sqrt(T))T), simulated CVs.

E12_false_alarm.v: No ARL0. Multiplicity across the recursive sequence explicitly discussed: the BSADF 'will be sure to identify a bubble if just given a sufficiently fine partitioned time series'; the GSADF's 'significance level applies to the entire time series and not just the subsections'; since the BSADF statistic has a distribution 'one could potentially correct for multiple testing as well'; the LPPL has no such correction (sec.4 pp.20-21, sec.2.1). False detection under the null quantified as detection rates in Table 2 cols [1]-[4] (GSADF 0.0320-0.7290; GSADF^B 0.0370-0.2330; LPPL0.1/0.05 ~1.0).

E13_validity.v: GSADF framework assumes an untested common unit root (cointegration) between price and dividend processes (sec.1 p.2). Null: P_t = T^-1 + P_{t-1} + eps_t, eps iid N(0,sigma^2), sigma=6.79, P0=100. Minimum window floor(T(0.01+1.8 T^-1/2)) = 19/27/40 observations for T=100/200/400 (PSY rule). Documented failures: GSADF oversized under serially correlated innovations (AR(1): up to 0.7290; MA(3): up to 0.4490), confirming Pedersen & Schutte (2017); sieve-bootstrap GSADF^B restores ~5% for serial correlation but BOTH GSADF and GSADF^B are oversized under GARCH innovations, worsening with T (0.1530->0.3220 and 0.1300->0.2330), contradicting PSY (2015) and in line with Harvey et al. (2016) wild-bootstrap findings (sec.6.1 pp.30-31). Bootstrap technicality: for the robust GSADF, collapse-point errors larger than 10 SD are replaced by iid draws of matching SD before resampling (sec.6.1 p.30); 199 bootstrap replications (MacKinnon 2002). LPPL procedure has no test statistic or null distribution - size/power undefined, detection driven by an arbitrary max-RMSE threshold (0.1/0.05/0.01) with no value that works across processes (sec.3-4, sec.8 p.39). Robustness: similar results for other volatilities and explosiveness magnitudes; T>400 computationally infeasible (sec.7 p.37).

E13_validity.v: Null (3): unit root with asymptotically negligible drift k*T^{-gamma}, gamma>1/2. Alternative model (2): delta_T = 1+c1*T^{-alpha}, c1>0, alpha in [0,1) (mildly explosive); collapse gamma_T = 1-c2*T^{-beta}, c2>0, beta in [0,1) (mildly integrated); errors iid (0,sigma^2). Appendix Assumption (EC): u_t = psi(L)eps_t linear process, sum j|psi_j|<inf, eps_t iid mean 0, variance sigma^2, finite fourth moment (extension to mds noted). Reverse-regression BSDF* statistic has noncentral limit distribution from endogeneity (Theorem 1). Dating consistency needs scv(T) within rate intervals e.g. (T^{alpha*beta/2}, T^{(1-alpha)/2}) depending on (alpha,beta) - more restrictive than PWY; harder as beta grows (slow collapse). Real-time reverse implementation needs small min window (~6 obs discussed; sims use f0 0.06-0.24). No non-stationary-volatility robustness analysis

Super-exponential tests: non-nested model selection of AR(1)-in-log-returns null vs fitted LPPLS trend A + (tc-t)^m [B + C cos(omega ln(tc-t) - phi)] with 0<m<1, B<0, 3<omega<15, |C|(omega^2+m^2)^{1/2} <= |B|m, or PL simplification A + B(tc-t)^m. Implementation: rolling windows of 60 quarters (max), tau0=0.2 (0.3 for super-exponential), minimum 12 quarters, serial correlation in residuals corrected; critical values from finite-sample MC (T=60, 15,000 reps). Reported limitations: LPPLS calibration difficult on quarterly data (7 parameters; >90% constraint failures at the 90% CV level); supDF's poor forecast skill attributed to the 60-quarter sliding window; joint-hypothesis problem acknowledged (differences may reflect theory or statistical power)

Generating models (5) (regime switch, no collapse) and (6) (collapse with re-initialization X_tau_f = X_tau_e + X*, X* = Op(1)); theory given for (6). Assumptions: eps_t iid (0, sigma^2) (extendable to weakly dependent errors via Phillips 1987 / PMb); X0 = Op(1); mildly explosive root rho_n = 1 + c/n^eta, c>0, eta in (0,1); r0 = 0.2 in simulations; tau_f - tau_e > log(n) duration separation; single episode assumed (repeated episodes claimed applicable, not proved). Non-zero intercept in the DGP during explosive episodes yields an empirically unrealistic dominating deterministic trend - theory assumes zero intercept in the generating mechanism (intercept allowed in unit-root periods with proof modification). Known caveat stated: large CV expansion rate causes overestimation bias in the origination date; post-collapse rho-hat has second-order downward bias (Remark (e)). Design: two-step PSY-window + HLS-BIC procedure vs PSY BSADF dating; six DGPs A-F from model (2)-(5), vt iid N(0,1), mu=0, N=2 (T=200) or N=3 (T=300); delta_j1 in {0.05, 0.075, 0.1} (explosive), delta_j2 in {-0.05, -0.075} (collapse), regime fractions as listed per DGP (e.g. DGP A: regimes (0.2,0.3,0.4) and (0.6,0.7,0.8), delta=(0.1,-0.05)); 10,000 retained replications (Gauss 18), ADF lag fixed at 1, conditioning on GSADF 5% rejection and upward regimes (y_tau2T > y_tau1T). E13_validity.v: DGP (1): four-regime model; H0: delta_iT=0 (unit root throughout); locally explosive alternative delta_iT = ci/T for power, mildly explosive c1 T^-alpha for dating. Assumptions: A1 eps_t = sigma_t z_t, z_t IID, mean 0, variance 1, E|z_t|^r < inf, r >= 4; A2 sigma_t = omega(t/T), non-stochastic, strictly positive, cadlag (countable jumps, trends, smooth transitions allowed); A3 density f continuous at 0, f(0)>0, bounded; A4 F(0)=1/2 (median zero - relaxed in sec.7 via recursive demeaning, invariant to E[sign(z_t)]); u1 = op(T^1/2); pi=0.1 minimum window (convention). Key validity results: sPSY/sPWY exactly invariant to sigma_t under H0 (no bootstrap needed); PSY/PWY limit null distributions depend on omega(s) - size not controlled with homoskedastic CVs (documented failure, Table 2); wild bootstrap first-order valid jointly for (PSY, sPSY) (Theorem 3); both statistic families numerically invariant to level mu (intercept-free variants PSY0/PWY0 severely mu-sensitive in finite samples, Table 6); sign tests robust to any finite number of arbitrarily large deterministic level shifts, PSY/PWY only to o(T^1/2) shifts; local drift mu + T^-d t: sign-based null limits hold iff d > 1/2 (same restriction as PSY/PWY); serial correlation handled by recursive AR(p) prewhitening (8), p by BIC, null limit unchanged; asymmetric errors handled by recursive demeaning at some power cost.

E13_validity.v: Continuous-time random coefficient system dy_t = (mu + sigma dW1/dt) y_t dt + gamma dW2 (model 2.2; endogeneity rho = corr(W1,W2) in model 5.1). Trajectory typology: unstable kappa = mu + sigma^2/2 > 0 (E theta^2 > 1), locally explosive mu > 0 (E theta > 1), explosive nu = mu - sigma^2/2 > 0; nesting STUR/NERC discrete models; localizing rate governed by sampling interval delta - no need to estimate a localization exponent alpha. Two-stage estimation (Phillips-Yu 2009): realized variance/quarticity within blocks (M obs per block, N blocks), then approximate MLE for mu. Asymptotics: double (T -> inf, delta -> 0) for mu (rate 1/sqrt(T), requires sqrt(T) delta -> 0 for CLT); infill (T fixed, delta -> 0) for (sigma^2, rho, gamma^2); t-statistics asymptotically N(0,1). Under endogeneity with long span, sigma and gamma not consistently estimable in explosive cases (signal domination); gamma^2 estimation poor when kappa > 0 (acknowledged, argued immaterial to the tests). Approximation error O(sqrt(delta)) drives finite-frequency size distortion. Gaussian driving Brownian motions; no fat-tail/volatility-misspecification robustness study; empirical caveat: endogeneity model avoided for daily data because rho estimation bias is severe in long-span low-frequency explosive samples (fn.9).

E13_validity.v: DGPs: (2.3) random walk switching at [n rc] to polynomial trend pnc + gamma (t-nc)^m + eps_t, m >= 2, eps iid mean 0, variance sigma^2, E eps^4 < infinity (extension to linear-process errors claimed via the 2017 WP version, fn.2; also robust to variants pt = pt-1 + gamma(t-nc)^(m-1) + eps and general polynomials, fn.3 and sec.6); (3.9) switch to mildly explosive 1 + gamma/ne^alpha, gamma>0, alpha in (0,1). Key asymptotics: AR(1) fit to polynomial trend: ns(rho-tilde - 1) ->p (2m+1)(m^2-1)/(2m^2) (= 15/8 at m=2) and ns^(-1/2) t ->p sqrt(4m^2 - 1) - both exceed right-tail CVs, so spurious explosiveness; AR(2) fit: (n2-n1)(rho-hat - 1) ->p 0 and t ->p 0 (m=2) or -infinity (m>2); under unit-root null the AR(2) statistics have exactly the PSY limit distributions, so PSY critical values remain valid. The proposal equals PSY's ADF regression with lag k=1 instead of the k=0 used empirically by PSY. Caveat: m=2 exactly matches the AR(2) representation; higher-order trends need AR(k) (Online Supplement). Homoskedastic errors; heteroskedasticity handled by citing HLZ/HLST literature, not analyzed here.

E13_validity.v: Null models: H01 with intercept vs H02: y_t = d T^-eta + y_{t-1} + eps_t, d-tilde=1 normalization (localizing exponent eta the sole drift determinant); asymptotic SADF distribution discontinuous at eta=0.5: F3(W, r0) for eta>0.5 (PWY-type Wiener functional) vs F4 (0<=eta<0.5, standard-normal-type functional dominated by deterministic trend); eta=0.5 boundary case depends on nuisance parameters d-tilde and sigma. Finite-sample distribution invariant to eta for eta>0.5, strongly eta-dependent below. CVs sensitive to r0 (95% F3: 1.39-1.57 as r0 falls 0.2->0.05). Alternative: Evans periodically collapsing bubble (eqs 12-14) with full parameterization; eta not a choice parameter and typically unknown - key practical caveat. Lag selection matters: BIC fine, sequential significance testing oversizes (fn.6). Errors iid N(0,1) in simulations; no heteroskedasticity analysis. Practical guidance: formulate the empirical regression with intercept but interpret against the appropriate null drift specification; deterministic trend handling changes limit theory.

E13_validity.v: DGP (1)-(2): four-regime model (unit root, explosive delta_1T, collapse delta_2T, unit root), local magnitudes delta_iT = di/T or fixed di; mu handled by demeaning; u1 = op(T^1/2). Assumption 1: eps_t = sigma_t z_t, z_t IID(0,1), E|z|^r < K, r >= 4; sigma_t = omega(t/T) non-stochastic, strictly positive, bounded cadlag (Cavaliere-Taylor class) - allows single/double shifts, smooth transitions, trends; conditional heteroskedasticity (GARCH) NOT covered by the non-stochastic assumption but discussed. Theorem 1: PWY null limit S depends on omega (non-pivotal). Wild bootstrap (Algorithm 1: y*_t increments = Delta y_t * w_t, w_t NIID(0,1)) replicates the volatility path; first-order valid (Theorem 2); consistent under fixed alternatives at polynomial rate (Theorem 3), with BIC-residual variant PWY*B restoring the exponential-rate-matching size-adjusted behavior (heteroskedastic case conjectured). Serial correlation: linear-process errors handled by ADF lag augmentation with 1/p + p^3/T -> 0 for PWY; bootstrap statistics need no augmentation (wild bootstrap annihilates weak dependence). Application: commodity prices 2000-2013 with pre-tests for stationary volatility (Table 3) and bootstrap p-values overturning several PWY bubble detections (Table 4).

E13_validity.v: New collapse mechanism: L-process (2)-(4) - martingale with a randomized-drift collapse regime whose downward drift Lt (constant L or L -> infinity) generates abrupt or slow sustained collapses; alternative comparator DGP (7) is the PSY/PS stationary-reversal collapse. Key analytic results: under (4) the DF t-ratio diverges to +infinity at Op(T^(1/2)) when the recursion spans normal-to-crash regimes (Theorem 1) - explaining why the right-tailed PSY test detects collapses; under (7) it diverges to -infinity (Theorem 2) - no right-tailed discriminatory power. Errors satisfy Assumption A1 or A2 (iid / weakly dependent, Appendix). r0 per PSY convention. Implication drawn: the L-process is the appropriate model for collapse detection by PSY-type tests; date-stamping consistent only under (4). Wild bootstrap recommended empirically for heteroskedasticity. No volatility-robustness simulation; homoskedastic simulations.

Detector: CUSUM of monitored observations vs historical mean, normalized by kernel long-run variance from the M-observation historical (training) sample (assumed change-free); boundary exponent gamma in [0, 1/2) (theory fails at 1/2); kappa=1/2 termination T=M. Practical notes: results stable across 5/10/30-minute frequencies; overnight returns immaterial for N > 60; nonmonotone limit distributions make one-sided testing direction consequential (six-scenario design, Table 1). Explosiveness-vs-bubble distinction maintained (no fundamentals at high frequency).
